problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Solve the following initial value problem:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Distinct Eigenvalues and Initial Conditions

feedback.problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that the position of a particle at time $t$ seconds is given by the vector $x(t),$ and that $x(t)$ is the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

find the position of the particle at $t=5$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ into the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2} \\ 2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=5 \\ 2{c}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{c}_{1}+2\cdot \frac{1}{2}=5\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=4.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution for the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate $x(5)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(5) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2\cdot 5} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{10} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+{e}^{10} \\ {e}^{10}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
